reason: I’ll start making the supporting material by connecting the copied instructions to the cell’s protein machinery.
expectation: I expect this to start collagen production, though amino acids and export machinery may still be needed.

alternatives.reason: The repair signals may activate nearby skin cells, but the current goal focuses on supporting material.

effect: The copied instructions direct ribosomes in local connective-tissue cells to make collagen; I’ll continue that process.
reaction: The link back to protein production in muscle cells makes the shared machinery clear.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks needed to make the supporting protein.
expectation: I expect the directed builders to assemble a collagen protein or an early form of it.

alternatives.reason: The signals may activate skin cells, but I want to finish the collagen pathway first.

effect: The amino acids supplied material for collagen chains, which enter processing membranes as they are made. I’ll continue toward supporting material.
reaction: The distinction between instructions and actual building material is clear.
reason: The new chains need processing and export to contribute to tissue outside the cells.
expectation: I expect the chains to be processed and exported as collagen, though further assembly may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Repair signals may help the skin cells respond, but I want to finish the collagen pathway first.

effect: The collagen material is processed and exported, then finished outside the cells to form supporting fibers. I’ll add those fibers to the damaged site.
reaction: It is interesting that cells help build the material around themselves.
reason: Adding the new fibers to the body seems like the next step toward supporting the damaged site.
expectation: I expect the fibers to provide support at the scrape, though the surface may still need rebuilding.

alternatives.reason: The signals may activate skin cells, but I want to use the supporting fibers first.

effect: The fibers now support the damaged region, and the next goal is to restore surface coverage.
reaction: The distinction between a temporary seal and rebuilt tissue is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the signals seem likely to start the skin cells' response.
expectation: I expect the signals to prompt nearby skin cells to help cover the scrape, though I don't know what form that response will take.

effect: The signals prompt nearby skin cells to move and multiply, providing living coverage that can be added to the rebuilding body.
reaction: It is useful to see that the signal guides repair but does not supply the replacement tissue.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should bring the surface cells to the damaged site.
expectation: I expect the spreading cells to cover the scrape, though the tissue may still need further repair.

effect: The surface barrier is restored, while deeper repair and strengthening continue; the patch may retain a scar.
reaction: The continuing repair makes the ending feel more realistic than an instant return to the original skin.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making and adding the supporting fibers connected protein production inside cells to rebuilding material around them.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the finished fibers to the body felt predictable after the preceding construction, though it showed where the material was used.

surprise.text: I was interested that cells export collagen material and helpers outside the cells finish processing it into fibers.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the compatible-partner menu made the sequence straightforward rather than a discovery of which parts fit.

continue.text: I would be curious to continue if another chapter explored a different body process; the connection between cell work and tissue repair held my interest, although several choices were predictable.
